community.headline: Grays social club bar manager to Brave the Shave for Macmillan
points: She has set up an online donation page
Club regulars have already given cash
community.summary: Kaz Frater, 50, will have her head shaved at the St Thomas of Canterbury Church Social Club on 14 November to thank the charity for its support to her family.

community.headline: Fancy dress Halloween walk wins Stanford school 7,200 Beat the Street points
points: Beat the Street turns towns into a game board for walking, cycling and rolling
Points help teams win prizes
community.summary: Families from Arthur Bugler Primary walked the area dressed as dinosaurs, minions, witches and pumpkins on Saturday, boosting the school's team in the activity game.

community.headline: Farleigh Hospice sets ten Light Up a Life services
points: Dunmow, Old Park Meadow: Thursday 26 November, 7pm
Braintree, George Yard: Wednesday 2 December, 6pm after a procession from the town hall
Chelmsford Cathedral: Sunday 6 December, 7.30pm
Donations can be dedicated to a loved one through the appeal
community.summary: Free remembrance services run from 26 November in Dunmow to 9 December in Maldon, Tollesbury and Boreham, with the main service at Chelmsford Cathedral on 6 December.

community.headline: St Luke's Hospice opens Light up a Life dedications
points: Basildon evening: Thursday 26 November, 6.30pm; Thurrock (Bulphan): Thursday 10 December, 6.30pm
RSVP for both by 20 November
Song dedications close 20 November for the show on Sunday 20 December
Pin badges have a suggested donation of £3.50
community.summary: The Basildon hospice will hold outdoor evenings of remembrance and a Gateway 97.8 song dedication show, with dedication boards in Eastgate and Grays shopping centres in December.

community.headline: Foodbanks ask families to fill a reverse advent calendar
points: Southend's calendar lists 24 items, to be dropped off by the first week of December
Southend collections are planned at Waitrose, Fossetts Way on 11 and 12 December
Southend is also seeking volunteers for supermarket collections
community.summary: Southend and Chelmsford foodbanks have launched 2026 reverse advent calendars, asking people to collect one item a day and donate them before Christmas.

community.headline: Essex charities urged to storm-proof buildings for winter
points: 8,344 non-residential properties in Essex are at high risk of surface-water flooding, Environment Agency data shows
Empty or rarely used premises are most at risk from frozen pipes and heating failures
Checklist includes keyholder contacts and a plan for where services could move
community.summary: A charity insurer says 1,633 Essex charities with buildings or open spaces should check roofs, drains and heating now, with a wetter, stormier early winter expected.

community.headline: 75,000 handmade poppies go on show for Chelmsford's first Poppy Festival
points: More than 200 people joined a knit-a-thon at the cathedral
Poppies arrived from as far as Australia
Remembrance service at the Duke Street war memorial at 10.55am on 8 November
community.summary: Volunteers from care homes, schools, knitting circles and faith groups made the poppies, now displayed at High Chelmer, the Indoor Market and South Woodham Ferrers.

community.headline: Southend Toy Drive returns for its 13th year
points: Runs until Tuesday 15 December
Volunteers sort and wrap the gifts
community.summary: New, unwrapped gifts are wanted for vulnerable children and young people in the city, with presents for older children and teenagers especially needed.

community.headline: Check bonfires for hedgehogs, urges Essex Wildlife Trust
points: Wrap bonfire bases in chicken wire to keep animals out
Skip sky lanterns, which can start fires on nature reserves
Clear up litter afterwards
community.summary: The trust's Bonfire Night advice: build or move bonfires on the day, light from one side and go to organised displays where possible.

community.headline: £2.5m project to rebuild Blackwater beaches for seabirds
points: Partners include RSPB, Harwich Haven Authority, Essex Wildlife Trust and ZSL
Aims to create nesting sites for little terns and ringed plovers
Restored beaches should also soften waves and cut flood risk
community.summary: Clean sand and gravel from Harwich harbour dredging will be reused to restore shingle at Cobmarsh Island and Old Hall Point instead of being dumped at sea.

community.headline: Peer support helped people attend 385 health appointments
points: More than 1,550 issues addressed in a year
Estimated £22,000 saved for the NHS
Six peer support workers, each supporting people over about 20 to 24 weeks
community.summary: A service run by EPUT and local charity SUMMIT in Colchester and Tendring helped people get to GP and hospital appointments and sort out issues such as housing and benefits.

community.headline: Harlow fundraiser brings South Asian community together for mental health
community.summary: MIND & Connect held a community event at Latton Bush Hall with food, crafts and clothing stalls, joined by Rainbow Services and Butterfly Wellbeing.

community.headline: Volunteers wanted to care for Thurrock Museum collection
community.summary: Helpers are needed to update the database and rebox some of the museum's 30,000 artefacts.

community.headline: Oncologist's concert raises £12,000 for cancer research
community.summary: A concert organised by a Southend Hospital oncologist has raised £12,000 for cancer research at the hospital.

community.headline: Council grants help Brentwood community garden flourish
community.summary: Brentwood Borough Council grants are supporting a local community garden.

community.headline: Work at Coalhouse Fort to protect wildlife and improve access
community.summary: Thurrock Council's Civic Pride programme is carrying out work at Coalhouse Fort aimed at protecting wildlife and opening up access.

community.headline: Poppy Appeal under way in Harlow
community.summary: Residents are being asked to support the Royal British Legion's Poppy Appeal in the run-up to Remembrance.

community.headline: Free youth clubs open in West Thurrock
points: Year 6 session 4pm to 4.55pm
Years 7 to 9 session 5.15pm to 6.15pm
Sport, crafts, gaming and snacks with qualified youth workers
community.summary: Purfleet charity Riverview Charitable Trust starts free Monday clubs at St Clement's Community Hall from 2 November.

community.headline: Freemasons' community fund passes £60,000 in five years
points: Fifth charity ball in Bulphan raised over £3,000
Focus on small, volunteer-led groups
community.summary: The Cross Keys Community Fund, set up by Essex Freemasons in Chadwell St Mary, has backed more than 150 local schools, care homes and groups.

community.headline: Essex Wildlife Trust photo contest marks its tenth year
points: Entries close at midnight on 30 November
Category winners shown at High Chelmer Shopping Centre
Overall winner picked by public vote in January
community.summary: Photographers of all ages can enter up to three Essex wildlife and landscape images taken in 2026, with a young people's category.

community.headline: Property dinner raises record £68,480 for air ambulance
points: More than 300 guests attended in September
Rightmove was headline sponsor
community.summary: The seventh Beresfords Property Dinner and auction brought in a record sum for Essex & Herts Air Ambulance.

courts.headline: Fly-tipper who dumped oil-filled barrels around Colchester given suspended sentence
points: 12-month suspended sentence and 200 hours of unpaid work
Ordered to repay £1,400 clean-up costs at £200 a month
The dumping happened in February and March 2025
courts.summary: Benjamin Perry admitted dumping blue barrels of used motor oil across the city and was sentenced at Ipswich Crown Court.

courts.headline: Parents jailed for more than 23 years for seriously harming a child
points: The man was jailed for 12 years and the woman for 11
Reporting restrictions prevent anyone involved being identified
courts.summary: A man and a woman were convicted of GBH with intent after a five-week trial at Ipswich Crown Court, a charge police described as rare in such cases.

courts.headline: Taxi driver jailed for five years over Langdon Hills passenger death
points: Sentenced at Basildon Crown Court on Wednesday 21 October
Banned from driving for seven and a half years
Cleared of murder and manslaughter after a 15-day trial
Michael Ashton, 28, died in October 2025
courts.summary: Hayadulla Turkmani, 53, of Hornchurch, was convicted of causing death by dangerous driving after his car struck a passenger he had just dropped off.

courts.headline: Rochford and Westcliff men jailed for drugs and a prohibited gun
points: Reddington jailed for 9 years 9 months
Mongan jailed for 8 years 8 months
Sentenced at Basildon Crown Court
Proceeds of Crime timetable set
courts.summary: Elliot Reddington, 36, and Joe Mongan, 27, admitted supplying cocaine and cannabis and possessing a prohibited firearm.

courts.headline: Second life sentence for Beshenivsky killer over gun plot
points: Tammy Rigg jailed for five years three months
Razzaq was convicted in 2006 over the robbery in which PC Sharon Beshenivsky died
Case heard at Harrow Crown Court
courts.summary: Faisal Razzaq, 45, was given life with a minimum of eight years for conspiring to sell banned guns; a woman who stored a converted firearm in South Ockendon was jailed.

courts.headline: Colchester man jailed for ten years for sexual assaults
points: Found guilty on 18 September of multiple sexual assaults over two years
Placed on the sex offenders register indefinitely
courts.summary: Daniel Mowle, 42, denied the offences but was convicted by a jury at Chelmsford Crown Court.

courts.headline: Jailed drug dealers stripped of more than £1m
points: Renoldi loses £430,330; Green loses £609,418
Renoldi was jailed for 21 years and Green for 17
Some of the money will go to Essex Community Foundation
courts.summary: Confiscation orders totalling £1,039,748 have been made against Simon Renoldi, 55, and Iain Green, 56, who were jailed in 2025.

courts.headline: Basildon shop thief jailed and banned from two stores
points: Two-year criminal behaviour order bans him from both shops
Ordered to pay £162.50 compensation
Offences committed while on a community order
courts.summary: David Pitcher, 47, admitted 11 thefts from a Tesco Express and a BP garage over the summer and was jailed for eight weeks by magistrates.

courts.headline: Two Harlow 21-year-olds remanded over replica gun, machete and drugs
points: Reilly also faces dangerous driving and police assault charges
Hamill has pleaded not guilty
Both remanded in custody, next due at Chelmsford Crown Court on 20 November
courts.summary: Dominic Reilly and Kayci Hamill face charges linked to an incident on Tumbler Road, Harlow, on 22 October.

courts.headline: Developer denies 30 highways charges over Old Harlow homes
points: Charges under the Highways Act 1980 over street works payments
Trial adjourned to 27 April 2027
courts.summary: Anderson Developments Limited pleaded not guilty at Chelmsford Magistrates' Court to charges brought by Essex County Council over works at Moor Hall Farm.

courts.headline: Southend county lines gang jailed after Operation Raptor
points: Sentenced at Luton Crown Court on 16 October
Line linked to supply of over 1kg of drugs
A pistol, cash and bladed weapons were seized in raids
courts.summary: Twelve people linked to the 'Mali' drugs line, run from Luton and dealing in Southend, have been sentenced, with ten jailed for more than 60 years in total.

courts.headline: Purfleet 19-year-old locked up for six robberies and a machete threat
points: Victims lost phones, a bank card, hats and an e-scooter
He was arrested minutes after threatening a man with a machete on Grays High Street
Restraining orders protect four victims for seven years
courts.summary: Kevin DaSilva was sentenced at Basildon Crown Court to 50 months in a young offender institution after admitting robberies in Grays and Tilbury.

courts.headline: South Ockendon man who reversed into a police car given 21 more months
points: He fled after ramming a police dog unit vehicle
He was later caught in Colchester after dragging an officer with his car
Banned from driving for two years and nine months
courts.summary: Ricky Patmore, 30, wanted on recall to prison, admitted dangerous driving and assaulting an emergency worker and was sentenced at Southend Crown Court.

official.headline: Women-only weights sessions launch at Dovedale on Wednesday
points: Dovedale: Wednesdays 6pm to 6.45pm from 4 November
£3 a session, or £30 for the block if booked before 4 November
CSAC sessions start on 11 January 2027
South Woodham Ferrers already runs Friday classes
official.summary: Chelmsford's leisure centres are starting a 12-week women-only resistance training course, with CSAC sessions to follow in January.

official.headline: Government orders Southend to put its draft Local Plan out to consultation
points: The council says it is taking legal advice on what the direction means
Publication does not mean the plan is adopted or final, the council stresses
The Local Plan website will be updated before consultation opens
official.summary: A letter from housing minister Matthew Pennycook directs the city council to publish its existing draft plan, with public consultation due to begin in early November.

official.headline: Epping Forest Community Lottery super draw offers PS5 Pro bundle or £1,000
points: Bundle includes a PS5 Pro, four games, a 50-inch 4K TV and a headset
Draws take place every Saturday at 8pm
Phone 01992 363016 to play without the internet
official.summary: Every normal £1 ticket bought by Saturday 28 November is entered into the super draw, with players choosing a local good cause to support.

official.headline: Maldon council ranked second in England for land charges records
points: The rating reflects accuracy of the register used by house buyers
Records cover planning decisions, tree preservation orders and legal restrictions
official.summary: The district has held a Gold Standard for four quarters in a row and sits second of 164 councils that have moved their local land charges to HM Land Registry.

official.headline: Vote for the new Springfield Green playground design
points: Residents can also name their favourite play equipment
Voting is online with a name and postcode
official.summary: Chelmsford City Council has put three designs for a replacement children's play area at Springfield Green to a public vote, closing at midday on Friday 6 November.

official.headline: Castle Point lists four Remembrance Sunday services
official.place: South Benfleet, Canvey Island, Hadleigh & Thundersley
points: South Benfleet: St Mary's Church from 10am, then the war memorial
Canvey: outdoor Royal British Legion service at The Paddocks from 10.40am, then a procession to Denham Road
Hadleigh: St James the Less from 10.50am, wreaths at the war memorial at noon
Thundersley: St Peter's Church from 10.50am
official.summary: Services will be held in South Benfleet, Canvey Island, Hadleigh and Thundersley on Sunday 8 November, each with a two-minute silence at 11am.

official.headline: Councillors lose power to call in smaller Castle Point planning cases
points: The council says the changes were imposed nationally, not chosen locally
It is concerned the rules reduce local democratic involvement
How applications are assessed, including residents' comments, is unchanged
official.summary: From 31 October, householder and minor applications are decided by officers under new national rules, and larger ones go to committee only if strict criteria are met.

official.headline: Free Health Compass wellbeing course returns at Runnymede
points: Mondays at 11am at Runnymede Leisure Centre, 16 November to 21 December
Ask your GP surgery or self-refer by emailing Wellbeing@castlepoint.gov.uk
Open to residents across the borough
official.summary: A six-week group programme on activity, diet, sleep and mental wellbeing, run with Benfleet GPs, starts its next series on 16 November.

official.headline: Up to 245 homes approved on former St Peter's College site
points: The planning committee approved it unanimously in early October
The county council is now looking at next steps for delivery
official.summary: Outline permission covers up to 185 new homes and up to 60 independent living homes for older people on the Chelmsford site designed by Essex Housing.

official.headline: More than a tonne of litter cleared from Colchester roadsides in October
points: Finds included tyres, old roadwork signs and two fly-tips
About 138kg was cleared from Weir Lane in 25 minutes with help from the MOD
official.summary: Street care crews collected over 1,100kg from verges and roads, including 710kg from a four-kilometre stretch of the A12 during a planned closure.

official.headline: Council-owned Amphora takes over Colchester grounds maintenance today
points: No savings figure has been published
official.summary: The council's own company replaces Idverde from 1 November, with savings expected compared with the old arrangement.

official.headline: New 62A and 62B buses link east Southend with the airport
points: The 62A runs seven days a week
The 62B adds weekday peak trips around the Stock Road area
Services began on 25 October
official.summary: Arriva's new routes, backed by the city council, run between Southend Travel Centre and London Southend Airport, with a bus about every 30 minutes on key sections.

official.headline: Dustfree Springfield and Vac Sparrow: Chelmsford names its new street cleaners
points: Shortlisted names included Dustbin Hoffman and Orlando Broom
official.summary: Residents sent in 128 ideas to name two compact sweepers and a jet tanker, with Anglia Dustin making up the winning trio.

official.headline: Twenty uninsured vehicles seized in Thurrock road operation
points: One driver was arrested on suspicion of drug-driving and driving while disqualified
Others were reported for phone use, seatbelts and careless driving
official.summary: Officers also reported 15 drivers for having no MOT during Operation Scalis on Friday 23 October.

official.headline: New LED street lights for Grays town centre
points: The council says the scheme came in on time and under budget
official.summary: Old columns and wall lanterns have been replaced, with better power for market traders and fittings for festive lights and banners.

official.headline: Solar panels fitted at Jaywick's Sunspot business centre
points: Paid for through the £20m Community Regeneration Partnership
official.summary: Tendring expects the panels to cut about 15 tonnes of carbon a year and save up to £10,000 a year in running costs.

official.headline: Epping community day marks Black History Month
points: Run by the Epping Forest Community Safety Partnership and a police advisory group
official.summary: Performances, speakers and competition prizes featured at the Civic Offices, with entries on display until 27 November.

official.headline: Family pay tribute to Westcliff cyclist, 72
points: Crash happened at about 4pm on Thursday 8 October
Family describe a devoted, animal-loving man and urge cyclists to wear helmets
Quote reference 0854 of 8 October when calling 101
official.summary: Steve Ames died in hospital on 22 October, two weeks after a crash involving a pedestrian in West Road. Police are still seeking witnesses and footage.

official.headline: Van more than 40% overweight stopped in Chelmsford
official.summary: Roads policing officers pulled over a van struggling along Colchester Road on the evening of 16 October and found it far above its weight limit.

official.headline: Smoke alarm warning after Basildon house fire
points: The house had no smoke alarms
Crews advise: get out, call 999 and stay out
Free smoke alarm fitting is available on 0300 303 0088
official.summary: A man returned home to find his semi-detached house full of smoke from a fire, believed to be electrical, that had smouldered for some time. He was taken to hospital for checks.

official.headline: Fire control handled 43,000 emergency calls last year
points: Crews attended almost 19,000 incidents in 2025/26
Incidents have risen 17% in five years
official.summary: Marking International Control Room Week, Essex Fire says its control team took almost 15,000 calls in July and August alone.

official.headline: Seven new on-call firefighters join Essex stations
points: On-call firefighters live or work within five minutes of their station
More than three quarters of Essex stations rely on on-call crews
official.summary: After two weeks of basic training in Witham, the recruits are heading to South Woodham Ferrers, Rochford, Manningtree, Braintree and Weeley.

official.headline: Ambulance control rooms took record 1.5 million 999 calls
points: About 500,000 more calls than the year before
Over 827,000 emergencies dispatched
Call handlers talked bystanders through CPR 8,489 times
official.summary: EEAST says its control rooms, including Chelmsford, answered calls in an average of two seconds in 2025/26, its busiest year on record.

official.headline: 800 people learn CPR at Colchester Zoo
points: About 80% of cardiac arrests happen at home
Fast CPR plus a defibrillator can more than double survival chances
official.summary: Ambulance staff and volunteers ran Restart a Heart Day sessions at the zoo on 16 October, teaching visitors CPR and how to use a defibrillator.

official.headline: Ambulance trust dismissals over sexual safety rise to 25
points: 156 sexual safety reports since April 2024
Trust says more people now feel able to come forward
An independent body is reviewing complaints procedures
official.summary: Councillors heard at an Essex health scrutiny meeting that EEAST dismissed 25 staff in 2025/26 over sexual safety cases, up from four the year before.

official.headline: Trading Standards seize 460,000 illicit cigarettes
points: About 238kg of hand-rolling tobacco seized
More than 9,000 illegal vapes taken off sale
Report concerns via Citizens Advice on 0808 223 1133
official.summary: Essex Trading Standards has taken part in Operation Machinize, a national crackdown on illegal tobacco and vapes linked to organised crime.

official.headline: Basildon sets out winter homelessness help
points: £85,000 to help 24 rough sleepers into shared homes
£12,000 for the BENS Winter Night Shelter
Residents worried about rent are urged to seek advice early
official.summary: The council has £312,582 from the national Rough Sleeping Programme for 2026/27, including money for a winter night shelter and severe weather beds.

official.headline: Braintree cost of living scheme worth £559,000 to residents
points: 600 electric blankets handed out this year
A further £400,000 committed over two years
Partners include Braintree Area Foodbank and community supermarkets
official.summary: The council's programme of 22 projects with local partners delivered an estimated £559,196 in benefits, debt relief and other help last year.

official.headline: Have your say on Southend transport plan to 2045
points: Drop-in at the Civic Centre on Tuesday 3 November, 11am to 2pm
Respond online via Your Say Southend
official.summary: The draft Local Transport Plan 4 covers walking, cycling, buses, roads and air quality. Consultation closes at 5pm on 17 November.

official.headline: New national rules change how Rochford decides planning cases
points: About 96% of Rochford applications already avoid committee
Councillors and parishes can ask for a gateway assessment within 21 days
official.summary: From 31 October, smaller applications must be decided by officers and councillors can no longer call schemes in to committee.

official.headline: Thurrock flu jab clinics and winter roadshows announced
points: Roadshow at Aveley Library on 4 November, 10am to 1pm
Free for over-65s, pregnant women and other eligible groups
official.summary: Catch-up clinics for children run in Corringham, Tilbury and Grays until 12 December, and Warm Up for Winter roadshows also offer jabs.

official.headline: Maldon invited to Armistice Day service at Hythe Quay
official.summary: The district council is inviting the community to mark Armistice Day at Hythe Quay.

official.headline: Revamped One Minet skate park opens in Saffron Walden
points: Opened Friday 30 October by Mayor Cllr Jeanette Curtis
Redesign shaped by a two-phase consultation with users
Works carried out by Betongpark
official.summary: The town council reopened the refurbished skate park with a ribbon cutting by the mayor and a coached skate session.

official.headline: Harwich council grant kicks off new youth and walking football groups
points: New Mini Shrimpers group for Key Stage 1 boys
New walking football group for mums and older women
Grant covers kit and the first 20 weeks of 4G pitch hire
official.summary: Harwich Town Council has given £1,275 to Harwich and Parkeston Youth Football Club to start two new groups.

also.name: Wivenhoe Town Council: Local Plan response

official.headline: Drop-in exhibition on Wednesday for 200 homes near Wivenhoe fire station
points: Up to 60 homes would be affordable, the developer says
The site is allocated in Colchester's draft Local Plan
The town council has objected to the allocation, saying it would harm a wildlife corridor and breach the Neighbourhood Plan
official.summary: Wates Manor Oak will show early plans for about 200 homes on land north west of the fire station at William Loveless Hall on 4 November, 3.30pm to 7.30pm.

official.headline: New Clacton, Holland and Jaywick councils pushed back a year to 2028
points: Clacton-on-Sea Town Council will have 25 councillors in eight wards
Holland-on-Sea Village Council will have 15 and West Clacton and Jaywick Sands 12
First councillors will serve a three-year term to line up with other parish elections
official.summary: Tendring's full council has agreed the three new community councils will start on 1 April 2028 rather than 2027, giving more time to prepare and consult residents.

official.headline: Pip Allam wins Great Bromley parish by-election
points: Turnout was 22.37%
official.summary: Pip Allam took 123 votes to Andrew Childs' 83 in the Great Bromley Parish Council by-election on 22 October.

official.headline: Seat open on High Ongar Parish Council
points: Requests go in writing to the Returning Officer at the Civic Offices in Epping
Otherwise the parish council will fill the seat by co-option
official.summary: A casual vacancy has arisen on High Ongar Parish Council. An election will be held only if ten local electors ask for one by 12 November.

official.headline: Green box recycling more than doubles under Tendring's new service
points: About 70,000 extra green boxes were delivered
Broken glass should not go in, and crews lift boxes by hand
official.summary: The weight collected from green boxes more than doubled in the first two weeks after glass, cartons and plastic pots were added on 5 October.

official.headline: Clacton Remembrance parade sets off from The Grove at 10.30am next Sunday
points: The Grove, Station Road, Pier Avenue and parts of Marine Parade will close temporarily
Manningtree's service is at 2.45pm at the High Street war memorial
official.summary: The parade on 8 November will march to the seafront Memorial Garden for an 11am service, with roads around the town centre closed for a time.

official.headline: Harwich roadshow offered autism awareness and free health checks
points: Partners included Essex County Council, the ICB and Essex Working Well
official.summary: A free workplace autism and health roadshow at Sentinel House included an autism reality bus, awareness training and NHS health checks.

official.headline: Thurrock's Remembrance season begins in Purfleet today
points: West Thurrock Memorial Park holds a short service at 2pm today
Grays hosts the civic service on 8 November and an Armistice Day service at 11am on 11 November
A free Armistice exhibition runs at the Thameside Complex until 12 November
official.summary: A parade from the Purfleet heritage centre at 10.15am and a service at St Stephen's Church open a fortnight of commemorations across the borough.

official.headline: Seven Thurrock roads resurfaced to extend their life
points: Other roads treated: Crofton Avenue, Humber Avenue, Lucas Road, Rookery Close and Rushdon Close
official.summary: Micro-surfacing has been laid on seven worn but sound roads, including Arkwright Road in Tilbury and Muckingford Road in Linford.

official.headline: 50 sacks of litter cleared on the A13 approach to Lakeside
points: 20 large items of debris were also removed in one shift
official.summary: Crews used an overnight closure at the A126 Dumbells Roundabout to cut grass and clear litter alongside National Highways works.

official.headline: Extra weekend night police patrols in Chelmsford city centre to run to Christmas
points: Patrols cover the High Street, Central Park and Bell Meadow
Summer patrols led to 10 arrests over 264 hours on foot
Paid for from the council's anti-social behaviour fund
official.summary: The council is paying for additional officers on Friday and Saturday nights, 7pm to 3am, through October, November and December.

official.headline: Southend's bin app shortlisted for a national recycling award
points: Downloaded more than 53,000 times
Shortlisted in a digital public engagement category
Winners due to be named later this year
official.summary: The Southend Resident Waste App, built with SUEZ and Cloud 9 Technologies, is in the running at the 2026 MRW National Recycling Awards.

official.headline: Southend consults on renewing and widening landlord licensing
points: Consultation open until 31 December on Your Say Southend
No final decision yet on which areas would be covered
There may be a gap between the old and new schemes
official.summary: The current scheme in parts of Milton, Kursaal, Victoria and Chalkwell wards ends on 30 November, and a larger replacement could start in April 2027.

official.headline: Work starts on turning three Clacton seafront buildings into micro venues
points: Part of a £20 million regeneration programme for Clacton and Jaywick Sands
Beach Patrol base due to be ready for the 2027 season
Public art hoarding expected around the site before the end of the year
A short stretch of path is shut, but step-free access from the Memorial Gardens remains
official.summary: An old shelter, former toilets and a storage hut above Kings Promenade are being converted into space for businesses and creative groups, with the Beach Patrol base below also being refurbished.

official.headline: Free housing advice day for Tendring tenants at the Princes Theatre
points: 10am to 2pm on 12 November at the Princes Theatre
Help on rent, the Housing Register, benefits, bills and adaptations
Free blood pressure checks and refreshments
official.summary: Council tenants and other households can meet the housing team and support groups in Clacton on Thursday 12 November, with no booking needed.

official.headline: Plans to bring Castle Park's Victorian boating lake back into use move forward
points: Detailed condition surveys will set the scope and final cost
The work will then go out to tender for a contractor
Spring 2027 target depends on surveys, procurement and approvals
official.summary: Colchester City Council is aiming to restore the 19th century lake in the Grade II listed park by spring 2027, once surveys, costs and approvals are settled.

official.headline: Another 9,500 Colchester homes are next in line for wheeled bins
points: Mixed recycling goes in one green-lidded bin with little sorting
Glass stays in the green box and food waste is still collected weekly
Rubbish and recycling collected on alternate weeks
Residents can check their start date with the council online tool
official.summary: The switch to wheeled bins continues in stages until March 2027, with more than half of Colchester households already on the new service.

official.headline: Last few days to comment on Braintree's Local Plan to 2043
points: Plan sets out where homes, jobs and infrastructure could go up to 2043
Documents online and in district libraries and Causeway House
Full Council decides in December whether to submit it for examination
official.summary: The final consultation on Braintree District's submission draft Local Plan closes at 5pm on Friday 6 November, the last chance for comments to reach the planning inspector.

official.headline: £225,000 upgrade for Hadleigh Country Park's two pump tracks
points: Both tracks keep their size but get new surfaces and layouts
Designed for riders of every ability
Work by specialist contractor On Track
official.summary: Essex County Council is resurfacing and redesigning both pump tracks for bikes, scooters, skateboards and skates, with work due to finish at the start of December.

official.headline: Southend parks team is selling real Christmas trees from £65
points: Four sizes from £65 to £100, stands £18 or £21
Delivery £5 to £20 to Rochford, Rayleigh, Benfleet and Basildon areas
Last orders on Tuesday 15 December
official.summary: Non-drop trees grown by the council parks team can be ordered online until 15 December, with free delivery inside the city.

stories.headline: Walsall end Colchester's unbeaten home league run
stories.summary: Colchester United lost 3-1 to Walsall in League Two, their first home league defeat of the campaign.

stories.headline: Late Wealdstone winner sinks Southend
points: Chambers-Parillon scored in the 5th and 39th minutes
Wealdstone replied through a penalty and a Luke Norris goal
stories.summary: Leon Chambers-Parillon put the Shrimpers ahead twice but Olufela Olomola struck in the 94th minute to give Wealdstone a 3-2 National League win.

stories.headline: Chelmsford City win 3-1 at AFC Totton
stories.summary: The Clarets picked up an away victory in National League South.

stories.headline: Colchester United owner on three bids since club went up for sale
stories.summary: Robbie Cowling told BBC Essex the club has had three potential buyers since he put it on the market in 2025.

stories.headline: ACA Harlow becomes Essex Cricket sponsor
stories.summary: The Harlow business has signed up as a sponsor of Essex County Cricket Club.

stories.headline: Chieftains hit Cardiff for seven to stay top
points: Ollie Baldock scored twice
Brandon Stones named man of the match
Chieftains top with 21 points from 8 games
stories.summary: Four goals in the second period set up a 7-2 home win over Cardiff Fire at Riverside.

stories.headline: Billericay put five past Hemel Hempstead
points: Chelmsford City also won, 3-1 at AFC Totton
Dagenham drew 0-0 at Maidenhead
stories.summary: Billericay Town ran out 5-0 winners at home in National League South, while Braintree edged Hampton & Richmond 1-0.

also.name: Safer Essex Roads: There Are No Respawns

stories.headline: Witham chef hit on a crossing by speeding driver backs young drivers campaign
points: The crash happened on a pedestrian crossing at Chipping Hill, Witham, on 17 August 2025
He suffered serious head injuries and broken bones in his pelvis, shoulder, collarbone, arm and finger
The driver, 22, of Witham, admitted dangerous driving offences and was jailed for two years in June
The campaign uses gaming language to warn young drivers there are no second chances
stories.summary: Fletcher Rice, 21, spent four months in a critical condition after a driver doing 53mph in a 30 zone hit him at Chipping Hill, and is now telling his story for the Safer Essex Roads 'No Respawns' campaign.

stories.headline: Business confidence in the East of England jumps to its highest level this year
points: Regional confidence rose 26 points to 62% in October
70% of firms are confident about their own trading outlook
A net 38% expect to take on more staff in the next year
The UK figure rose to 47%
stories.summary: Firms across the region reported a sharp rise in optimism in October, according to the monthly Lloyds Business Barometer.

stories.headline: Essex, the 'witch county', saw far more trials than Salem
points: 107 people were executed and 47 died in prison in Essex between 1542 and 1736, the museum says
More than 800 people were charged with witchcraft in the county over two centuries
15 women were tried and executed in Chelmsford in 1645, when Matthew Hopkins was active
Memorials now stand at Colchester Castle and in Chelmsford, and Tendring has a witch heritage trail
stories.summary: Historians say Essex held more witchcraft trials and executions than anywhere else in England, with the Essex Witch Museum putting the toll at more than five times that of Salem.

stories.headline: Nine in ten Harlow homes in line for £100 energy payment
points: That is 88.3% of Harlow homes, against 80.8% across England
Direct Debit council tax payers need do nothing; others will be invited to apply
Only the council will make contact about claiming, so treat other messages as scams
Help for bands E to H depends on a discretionary fund Harlow has yet to set out
stories.summary: The Budget's £100 household energy payment, due from January 2027 for council tax bands A to D, covers 35,870 of Harlow's 40,610 homes.

stories.headline: Harlow crime and anti-social behaviour reports up a quarter this summer
points: July 2026 was the busiest month in two years with 1,139 reports
Anti-social behaviour reports rose 66% over the summer and burglary was up 44% across the year
Shoplifting and vehicle crime both fell over the year
Harlow Council's Scrutiny Committee discusses a community safety review on Tuesday 3 November
stories.summary: An analysis of police.uk data found 3,303 reports in Harlow between June and August, 25% more than the same months of 2025, ahead of a council scrutiny meeting on community safety.

stories.headline: Harlow MP seeks answers as Poundland heads towards administration
points: The MP wants the owners to explain why an offer to save the chain was turned down
The Prime Minister called it a deeply worrying time for staff
Affected workers can contact the MP's office for help
stories.summary: Chris Vince says he is deeply concerned for staff at Poundland's large Harlow depot and two town shops, and has raised the local impact with the Business Secretary.

stories.headline: Brentwood offers Post Office temporary home in the Baytree Centre
points: The counter is due to close on 5 January and the shop on 12 January
Nothing has been agreed and the Post Office has not decided on a replacement
The council will also help the Post Office look for a permanent High Street site
stories.summary: The borough council has offered units until April 2028 after TG Jones, which hosts the town's Post Office counter, confirmed its Brentwood store will close.

stories.headline: Two held after homemade devices found in Brentwood street
points: Police were called at about 7.20am on Friday 30 October
Three small homemade explosive devices were found and made safe
A man and a woman, both in their 40s and from Brentwood, were arrested on suspicion of Explosive Substances Act offences
Residents were offered shelter at King George's Playing Fields pavilion
stories.summary: Around 40 homes in Sawyers Grove were evacuated on Friday while bomb disposal experts examined items found at a house. The cordon has since been lifted.

stories.headline: Brentwood man charged over Purleigh crash that killed passenger, 21
points: Thomas Chapman, 21, of Brentwood died at the scene at about 2am on 6 January
Mr Barnes first appeared at Colchester Magistrates' Court on Friday 30 October
He is next due at Chelmsford Crown Court on 27 November
stories.summary: Henry Barnes, 23, faces charges of causing death by dangerous driving and drink driving after a single-vehicle crash on Hackmans Lane in January.

stories.headline: Halloween dispersal orders in force across Essex this weekend
points: Canvey order runs from 4pm Friday 30 October to 4pm Sunday 1 November
It covers the High Street, Furtherwick Road, Eastern Esplanade, the sea wall and surrounding roads
Officers can direct anyone behaving anti-socially to leave the area
In Colchester the order covers Shrub End, Greenstead and Stanway from 4pm Saturday to 4pm Sunday
stories.summary: Police have extra powers to move people on in parts of Canvey, Colchester and Braintree to curb anti-social behaviour over Halloween.

also.name: BBC News: the homes row brewing in the town with no plan

stories.headline: Basildon chooses court fight over housing plan after minister's warning
points: Housing minister Matthew Pennycook wrote to the council on 26 October
A last-minute amendment replaced a planned vote to withdraw the plan
Labour councillors walked out without voting, and Labour has said it may consider legal action
Leader Andy Barnes can start proceedings if advised to
stories.summary: Basildon Council will seek a judicial review over its local plan deadline, keeping withdrawal of the 29,000-home plan only as a last resort after the housing minister said pulling it would be unlawful.

also.name: BBC News: so what now for local councils?

stories.headline: Decision on Essex council shake-up now due by early 2027
points: Southend backs a five-unitary model and says it will keep making that case
Thurrock's leader urged the government to give clarity sooner rather than later
Colchester is preparing charter trustees to protect its city status and mayoralty if the council is abolished
stories.summary: Ministers have confirmed reorganisation plans for other counties but say a decision on how Greater Essex is carved up will come by early 2027, after they weigh the representations received.

stories.headline: Colchester plans to keep its mayor and city title if council goes
points: Charter trustees are already used in Bath, Chester, Durham and Harrogate
Colchester's first royal charter dates from 1189
City status was granted in September 2022
stories.summary: A report going to councillors on 3 November recommends charter trustees to hold Colchester's city status, civic mayor and regalia should reorganisation abolish the city council.

stories.headline: Orsett minor injuries unit moves to Thurrock Community Hospital
points: Patients should head to Thurrock Community Hospital from Monday
stories.summary: The minor injuries unit at Orsett Hospital is relocating and opens at Thurrock Community Hospital in Grays on Monday 2 November.

stories.headline: Medieval Southchurch Hall to close for £423,000 restoration
points: Funded by Arts Council England's MEND programme
Work also covers drainage and refurbished visitor toilets
The hall dates from the mid-14th century
stories.summary: The Grade I listed moated manor house in Southend shuts to visitors from 1 November and is expected to stay closed until mid-2027 while its roof, windows and stonework are repaired.

stories.headline: Five men reported and dogs seized over Dengie hare coursing
points: Five men in their 20s and 30s will be reported under the Hunting Act 2004
Each was given a three-year community protection warning
Three more people are due to be interviewed
Rural residents are urged to call 999 if they see coursing in progress
stories.summary: Police seized four dogs and four vehicles after reports of hare coursing on the Dengie marshes on Wednesday morning.

stories.headline: Harlow man accused of conspiracy to steal £188,000 of flour
points: He appeared before Chelmsford magistrates
No plea has been indicated
Next due at Chelmsford Crown Court on 18 November
stories.summary: Erol Mustafa, 37, is charged with conspiring to steal flour from his employer, G R Wright and Sons, between July 2022 and January 2023.

stories.headline: Plans for 40 homes on Bulphan green belt fields
points: Applicant argues the land now counts as grey belt
Scheme includes 134 new trees, two ponds and a new link road to Old Church Hill
No decision date has been set
stories.summary: An outline application to Thurrock Council seeks up to 40 homes, half of them affordable, at Little Malgraves off Lower Dunton Road.

stories.headline: 159 homes approved for Tollesbury despite 724 objections
points: Plan by Welbeck Strategic Land IV approved on Wednesday 28 October
The planning report recorded 724 objections
Priti Patel MP was among those opposing the scheme
Residents raised traffic and narrow pavements on North Road
stories.summary: Maldon District Council's planning committee has backed a large housing scheme on land north of West Street in Tollesbury, despite strong opposition in the village.

stories.headline: Thurrock adopts new flag policy, ending Pride and Ukraine flags at civic offices
points: The borough coat of arms, Union Flag and St George's Flag will fly at the Civic Offices in Grays
Tilbury Civic Square will fly the Canadian Flag too, recalling Canadian troops stationed there in the First World War
Leader Richard Bingley says the policy is about civic pride
The policy also sets a process for marking civic occasions and commemorations
stories.summary: Thurrock's Reform-led council has set out which flags will fly at its Grays offices and in Tilbury, and the Pride and Ukrainian flags are no longer allowed.

stories.headline: c2c boss apologises as Purfleet and Rainham stay shut after derailment
points: GBR Anglia's Rob Mullen recorded a video apology to passengers
Signalling, cabling and track need rebuilding, which he called a major undertaking
Passengers from Grays as well as the three closed stations are asked not to travel
Replacement buses run between Upminster and Grays via Rainham and Purfleet
stories.summary: Trains will not stop at Dagenham Dock, Rainham or Purfleet until at least the week of 9 November while about 1.2km of track damaged in the Barking freight derailment is rebuilt.

stories.headline: Thurrock looks for lasting fix to Tilbury roads that keep cracking and sinking
points: Work on Cooper Shaw Road last September has already failed in places
The council blames ground conditions and heavy lorry traffic
It declined to say how much has been spent on repairs over two years
stories.summary: Repairs to Cooper Shaw Road and Fort Road have already cracked and subsided, and the council hopes to deliver a more substantial solution in 2027.

stories.headline: Grays has more than 50 of Thurrock's 172 licensed shared houses
points: Tilbury has 25 entries and Stanford-le-Hope 18
13 entries had re-licensing dates that have passed, seven of them in Grays, though they may have been renewed
The council links clusters to transport, amenities and jobs
stories.summary: The council's register of houses in multiple occupation lists 54 entries in Grays, followed by Tilbury and Stanford-le-Hope.

stories.headline: Smoking in Essex falls to lowest level on record
points: The council credits local stop-smoking services
The county is aiming to be smoke-free by 2030
Rates remain higher in the most deprived communities
Free stop-smoking aids and coaching are offered through the Essex Wellbeing Service
stories.summary: The share of adults who smoke in Essex has dropped from 11% to 9.2% on the latest three-year figures, the county council says.

stories.headline: Cyprus Airways to fly daily from Stansted to Larnaca from April
points: Tickets are on sale through the Cyprus Airways website
stories.summary: The airline will start a year-round daily route between London Stansted and Larnaca on 23 April 2027.

stories.headline: Southend sets up its first Music Board to back local talent
points: Chaired by music writer Daryl Easlea
Aims to give the scene a clear identity rooted in the city's musical history
Focus on helping new and emerging performers
stories.summary: The city council has launched a board drawing on figures from the music business to bring together Southend's scattered scene and champion emerging artists.

stories.headline: Four-home plan for Fobbing green belt follows dismissed appeal
points: One three-bed, two four-bed and one five-bed home, plus 12 parking spaces
Existing chalet bungalow would stay
Inspector dismissed the five-home appeal on 2 October but judged the site grey belt
stories.summary: A revised bid for four houses off High Road, Fobbing has gone to Thurrock Council weeks after an inspector threw out an appeal for five on the same land.
